label: copy-phase (post-delimiter) steps
explanation: Fires on almost every copy-phase step (t > L, from the second output on), at about a 93% rate, with flat rates across recall_idx, L, and input/output token identity. It is essentially silent during the original phase and at the <DEL> step: those hold about 0.04% of the mass, with only rare weak firing on repeated tokens late in the original phase. In the top examples, activation is lower at copy steps whose input is k (repeated-k sequences reach about 0.1-0.5 of max), but excluding k does not improve F1. The inactive copy steps (7% false positives) are scattered and show no clear pattern.

issues: The scores reproduce on the test split for 'phase == 2': precision 0.930, recall 0.9986, F1 0.963, mass recall 0.9996. Outside the copy phase it is nearly silent: 0.1% rate in the original phase and 40 of 500k delimiter steps, which agrees with the explanation.

There is one systematic counterexample class: copy-phase steps whose input is 'k'. On dev, other input tokens fire 93-97% of the time when phase==2 (a .947, b .957, d .936, t .931, 0 .971, 2 .934), but in_tok=='k' fires only 52.9% (test 53.1%, about 91k steps). That is roughly 43k of the 190k test false positives, about 23%, all in one token. The gap holds whether or not prev_tok is k (.517 vs .529) and on the last step (.505 vs .534 for to_go > 0). It is partly reversed when out_tok is also k (.742).

This contradicts the explanation's claim that the rate is 'flat across input/output token identity'. The explanation also understates the k effect as 'lower activation in the top examples'. In fact it is a firing-rate drop from about 94% to about 53%, not just a lower magnitude.

Excluding k does not improve F1 (phase==2 & in_tok!=k: test precision 0.944, recall 0.980, F1 0.9615 vs 0.963), so the original predicate stays the best simple one. The label is fine in essence, but the stated claims need correcting.

After removing k, the remaining false positives in the test misses look scattered across tokens, positions and L, with no other clear class. Missed activations (3.5k, original phase) carry about 0% of the mass.
